body:
## Pull request overview

This PR extends the ObjectStack protocol schemas to better support metadata-driven enterprise app development (Salesforce/ServiceNow-style), adding missing configuration surfaces across Data/UI/Automation/System/Security, along with accompanying validation tests.

**Changes:**
- Adds new protocol properties for UI views (quick filters, default related-list sorting), dashboards (global date range), and actions (visual variant).
- Adds new protocol properties for data modeling (field grouping & conditional required, object display name & record naming, validation priority, hook condition, datasource SSL).
- Adds new protocol properties for automation and governance (flow error handling, workflow execution order, approval escalation), plus i18n validation messages and tab visibility permissions.

### Reviewed changes

`errorHandling` docs say `maxRetries` is "only for retry strategy", but the schema currently allows `maxRetries`/`retryDelayMs` for any `strategy` value. This makes the contract ambiguous for consumers; consider enforcing conditional fields via a discriminated union (by `strategy`) or a `superRefine` that rejects retry-only fields when `strategy !== 'retry'` (and similarly requires `fallbackNodeId` when `strategy` needs it).

`escalation.enabled` defaults to false, but `timeoutHours` is required whenever `escalation` is present. This means you can't include `escalation: {}` (unlike other `enabled`-style configs in the repo) and the `enabled` default provides little value. Consider either (a) making `timeoutHours` optional and requiring it only when `enabled: true`, or (b) removing `enabled` and treating presence of `escalation` as "enabled".

`displayNameField` is described as defaulting to "name" if present, but the schema does not apply any default/transform (it will remain `undefined` unless explicitly set). Either implement a transform/defaulting behavior (if desired) or adjust the description to avoid implying behavior that validation/parsing does not provide.
```suggestion
  displayNameField: z.string().optional().describe('Field to use as the primary record display label in UI contexts (e.g., "name", "title").'),
```

`recordName.startNumber` allows `0` (`min(0)`) but the description says default is 1. Also, no `.default(1)` is applied, so omitted values won't become 1 at parse-time. Please align the constraint/description with the intended behavior (e.g., require `min(1)` and/or clarify that the runtime will supply the default rather than the schema).
```suggestion
    startNumber: z.number().int().min(1).optional().default(1).describe('Starting number for autonumber (default: 1)'),
```
